rule: This file is written BEFORE the measuring run. Every figure in it is a PREDICTION. A miss is recorded, never edited.
the_fix: A redirect turns `move.smartTarget` OFF, so a redirected Dragon Darts stops splitting and both darts land on the redirector. `Pokemon#getMoveTargets` runs `priorityEvent('RedirectTarget')` at sim/pokemon.ts:836 and only calls `getSmartTargets` at :838 if the flag survives — and all four legal redirectors clear it: followme (data/moves.ts:6065), ragepowder (:14617), lightningrod (data/abilities.ts:2346), stormdrain (:4641).
the_derivation_was_wrong_first_and_the_p: The first version of this wire was going to be 'a MOVE-sourced redirect clears the flag, an ABILITY-sourced one does not'. tests/probe_smart_target_redirect.js reads the four blocks out of the authority's own text on every run and went RED on that claim BEFORE any engine line was written. The rule is simpler than the one I had: every redirector clears it. That check stays in the probe rather than being written down once, because a regulation that changed one of the four would otherwise leave the comment describing an engine nobody has.

the_one_game_named_before_the_run.what: Rage Powder is up on Volcarona. Dragapult's Dragon Darts is drawn onto it; the authority puts BOTH darts into Volcarona (65/160 then 31/160, with the Sitrus settled between the two by the in-loop Update). medicham2 split them and sent the second into Rotom-Wash, 56/125 -> 1/125, a body the authority never touched.

predicted_after.counters: MEDSEEN.smartTargetSplitRefusedByRedirect non-zero AND MEDSEEN.smartTargetSplit still non-zero on the pinned pool — the pair is what says this scoped the flag rather than deleting the mechanic

why_it_might_miss_HIGH: Rage Powder carries 13,785 sheets and Dragon Darts 229, so the pair is rare but the redirect is not. A redirected dart landing on a DIFFERENT body changes every draw after it, so a game that currently agrees could part somewhere new — the same shape as the step-3 miss, where the named cause closed and the game re-parted on a Leftovers residual ordering.
why_it_might_miss_LOW: The named game may carry a second defect behind this one, in which case board-material lands at 42.
not_claimed: `wonderguard.onTryHit` (data/abilities.ts:5551) clears the same flag on an IMMUNITY and suppresses its own `-immune` line when it does. That is a different question and is NOT wired here.
